title: If police stop or question you
body: Stay calm and polite. You can ask why you are being stopped or questioned. Note the officers' names, vehicle number, time and place. You may ask to contact a family member or a lawyer. Do not argue physically and do not sign papers you do not understand.
steps: Note officer names, time and place
Ask to contact family or a lawyer

title: If you are arrested or detained
body: If you are arrested, stay calm and do not resist physically. Ask the reason for the arrest. You may ask to inform a family member and to consult a lawyer. Do not sign any document you do not understand. Remember the police station name, time and officers' details.
steps: Ask to call family or a lawyer

title: How to register an FIR
body: An FIR (First Information Report) is the first record of a criminal complaint at a police station. Go to the police station of the area where the incident happened, explain the facts clearly and ask for a copy of the FIR. Keep the copy safe.
steps: Go to the relevant police station

title: If police refuse to register an FIR
body: If police refuse to register your FIR, ask for the reason. You may contact a lawyer, a legal-aid organization or the relevant police complaint authority. Keep evidence such as messages, photos, names, dates and witnesses. Stay calm and document everything.
steps: Contact a lawyer or legal aid
Keep a record of your visits

title: Bail basics after arrest
body: Bail is a legal process to seek release from custody while a case continues. A lawyer usually files the application in the relevant court. Keep the FIR copy, arrest details and court notices safe, and do not miss court dates. Contact a licensed advocate urgently.
steps: Ask your lawyer about the bail process

title: Workplace harassment options
body: If you face harassment at work, save evidence: messages, emails, dates, names and witnesses. Check whether your workplace has a harassment policy or complaint committee. You may also report to the relevant authority or consult a lawyer.
steps: Report to the committee or authority

title: Street harassment and immediate safety
body: If you feel unsafe, move to a crowded, well-lit place and call someone you trust. Save evidence such as messages, screenshots or a vehicle number if it is safe to do so. In danger, use the SOS feature and consider calling the police emergency number.
steps: Move to a safe crowded place

title: If you face domestic violence
body: If you are in immediate danger, move to a safe place if possible and contact someone you trust. Save evidence such as messages, photos of injuries, medical records and dates when it is safe. You may seek help from a lawyer, a women-protection service or a legal-aid organization.
steps: Seek a lawyer or protection service

title: Online fraud or scam
body: If you were scammed online, stop further payments and do not share codes. Save screenshots of the profile, chat, receipts and transaction IDs. Report the account to the platform and consider reporting to the relevant cybercrime authority. Change passwords and enable two-factor authentication.

title: Cyber harassment or hacked account
body: If someone harasses you online or your account is hacked, do not engage. Take screenshots with dates and usernames, block and report the account, change your password and enable two-factor authentication. For serious threats or blackmail, save evidence and consult a lawyer.
steps: Consult a lawyer for serious threats

title: Consumer complaint basics
body: If a product or service is faulty, keep the receipt, warranty, photos and messages with the seller. Ask the seller in writing for a refund or repair. If they refuse, you may complain to the relevant consumer forum or authority. Keep copies of everything.

title: Unpaid salary or unfair termination
body: If your salary is unpaid or you were terminated unfairly, keep your contract, salary slips, attendance record and messages. Politely ask the employer in writing for the pending amount. If it is not resolved, consult a lawyer or the relevant labour authority.
steps: Consult a lawyer or labour authority
